title: microstutter-latency-profile-flash-paged-fusedops
content:
Purpose:
This is an investigation notebook focused on microstutter (p95/p99 latency spikes) observed in recent canary runs when we switched to the fused-op execution path for Llama-2-family models. We compare FlashAttention, paged attention, and the fused-ops variant across representative production-like workloads.

Summary Findings (up front):
- FlashAttention gives best median token throughput for long-sequence steady-state workloads, but we observed recurring p99 spikes (~2-4x p50) under bursty small-sequence traffic.
- Paged attention reduces memory pressure and avoids OOMs on constrained nodes, and reduces variance for short sequences. However, paged attention introduces additional per-request overhead (page management + prefetching) that hurts p50 for medium-length sequences (256-1024).
- The fused-ops runtime path reduces some kernel launch overheads and improves overall throughput for dense micro-batches, but interacts poorly with our async KV cache eviction and causes lock contention leading to stuttering at high concurrency.

Repro environment:
- Hardware: Giga-Cluster-3 nodes: 8x A100-40GB (fw: 510.73), small test on 2x H100 (fw: 515.85) for sanity checks.
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.2, cuDNN 9.6 (same as prod images).
- Runtime: redwood-serving 1.14.2-rc, inference-runtime compiled with --use_fast_kernels, --enable_paged_attention feature flag.
- Models: rwd-llama2-13b-v2 (fp16), rwd-llama2-70b-8k-quant (q4f16), also synthetic benchmark with random weights for isolating kernel performance.
- Load generator: redwood-loadgen v0.9 (closed-loop), mixes: small-chat (mean seq=64, bursty keys), long-doc (mean seq=2048, steady).

Test matrix (executed automated runs):
- Kernels: [FlashAttention, PagedAttention, FusedOps]
- Batch sizes: [1, 4, 8, 16]
- Concurrency: [1, 8, 32, 64]
- Seq lengths: [32, 64, 256, 512, 1024, 2048]
- KV cache modes: [none, local-kv, remote-kv]
- Quantization: [fp16, q4f16]

Representative command snippets (for reproducibility):
- baseline run (flash): ./run_infer --model rwd-llama2-13b-v2 --batch 8 --seq 512 --kernel flash --kv local --threads 8 --profile nvtx --output perf_flash.json
- paged run: ./run_infer --model rwd-llama2-13b-v2 --batch 8 --seq 512 --kernel paged --prefetch true --profile nvtx --output perf_paged.json
- fused path: ./run_infer --model rwd-llama2-13b-v2 --batch 8 --seq 512 --kernel fused --fuse-linear true --profile torchprof --output perf_fused.json

Profiling tools used:
- nvprof / NVIDIA Nsight Systems for kernel timelines
- torch.profiler for operator breakdowns in fused vs unfused paths
- eBPF + BPFTrace for spin/wait detection on CPU threads (lock contention)
- custom in-runtime wall-clock timers (per-request, per-token) with NTX counters exported to Prometheus

Key observations (detailed):
1) FlashAttention median vs tail:
- For long-doc steady workloads (seq>=1024), flash shows best p50 and highest token/sec. Example: seq=2048, batch=4: flash p50=18 ms/token, paged p50=26 ms/token, fused p50=17 ms/token.
- For small-chat (seq~64), flash p50=6 ms/token but p99 jumps to 32 ms/token in bursty open-loop tests. Root cause appears correlated with page faults on GPU memory when multiple requests concurrently allocate/deallocate temporary buffers (see kernel timeline).
- NVTX shows flash_attn_forward kernels are very fast but interspersed with long gaps where CPU stalls waiting on device-side page migrations.

2) Paged attention behavior:
- Predictable memory footprint: consistent peak GPU memory ~60% for seq <=512 where flash reached ~85% and triggered eviction.
- Overhead: extra ~1.8-2.4ms per forward for page-table management and async prefetch. This is visible at seq=256 where paged p50 > flash p50. But p99 is much tighter: paged p99 ~ 1.3x p50 vs flash p99 ~ 4x p50 for bursty small-chat.
- With prefetch disabled, p95/p99 degrade due to on-demand page faults. Prefetch tuning reduces tail but increases p50. There's a useful sweet spot for prefetch_window=2 for our workload mix.

3) Fused ops interactions and lock contention:
- Fused path reduces kernel launches for linear->gelu->linear stacks. Torch profiler shows ~12% fewer operator calls and 9-12% lower total kernel time at steady state.
- However, fused path triggers a hot path in the runtime where tensor metadata allocation uses a central pool lock. Under concurrency >=32, eBPF traces show >150k mutex attempts/sec on the tensor-pool lock, with many tasks spinning for 200-400us causing microstutters.
- Root cause: the fused executor reuses intermediate buffers more aggressively; the buffer pool implementation wasn't updated to be shard-friendly.

4) KV cache eviction and async flushes:
- In local-kv mode, when cache size approaches threshold (set by --kv-max-bytes), the eviction thread kicks in. Flash attention workloads with large past-key-values provoke eviction while forward is active, causing occasional stalls as the eviction synchronizes with the GPU stream.
- Paged attention isolates this somewhat because it keeps a smaller resident footprint; fused path exacerbates it since buffer reuse leads to eviction of buffers still referenced by async CUDA streams.

Microbench table (excerpted numbers from consolidated runs):
- Model: 13B fp16, batch=8, seq=512, concurrency=32
  - Flash: p50=12.8ms, p95=28.4ms, p99=52.9ms, mem_peak=33.1GB, tokens/s=68k
  - Paged: p50=17.6ms, p95=23.1ms, p99=31.7ms, mem_peak=22.8GB, tokens/s=51k
  - Fused: p50=11.9ms, p95=35.2ms, p99=64.5ms, mem_peak=31.2GB, tokens/s=72k

Interpretation:
- Fused gives best p50/tokens but worst tail due to lock contention + eviction interactions.
- Flash has good median for long sequences, but is brittle under bursty small requests due to temporary buffer allocations and page migrations.
- Paged is the safest for tail and memory-limited nodes; costs some median throughput.

Short, practical mitigations tried (and results):
- Sharded buffer pools: Implemented a quick patch to make buffer pools per-thread (hash by thread id) instead of global. Result: reduced mutex contention (~85% fewer mutex attempts), fused p95 improved from 35ms -> 21ms in a follow-up run. Still seeing residual p99 spikes under extreme concurrency.
- Eviction backoff: Add exponential backoff to the eviction thread when CUDA streams are busy. Result: reduced occurrences where eviction waited on forward, p99 flash decreased by ~18%.
- Prefetch window tuning for paged attention: window=2 gave best p99/p50 balance for mixed workload.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Are page-migration stalls observed with Flash attention a kernel-level bug in our allocator, or a property of the CUDA driver when many ephemeral buffers are created? Need Nsight rocket-prof trace and driver logs to confirm.
- For fused path: can we make the buffer pool lock-free or epoch-based reclaim rather than mutex-protected? Need engineering time estimate.
- Test H100-specific kernels (cutlass/fwd variants) — initial H100 tests show similar trends but lower absolute tail; we should run full suite on H100 before changing default kernel selection.
- Investigate per-request affinity: pinning forward worker threads to specific NUMA/cpu cores reduced CPU-side stalls in one experiment. Should we enforce core pinning in runtime?

Action items (who/when):
- Jinwoo: collect full Nsight Systems trace for a reproduced p99 flash spike (deadline: 2026-03-05).
- Ethan: prototype a lock-free buffer pool or adopt folly::MPMC queue for freelist (prototype by 2026-03-12).
- Aisha: run H100 batch of full test matrix and summarize differences (by 2026-03-08).
- Sofia: update canary config to use paged attention for memory-constrained tiers and monitor tail metrics next 2 weeks (by 2026-03-04).

Notes to self (scratch):
- Remember to include PR/issue links for fused buffer pool change: PR-874 touched this area last quarter.
- Check that quantized kernels (q4) may bypass fused path — need to add q4 runs to next test.

[ts 1612345678.123] thread=worker-27 mutex=buffer_pool_lock try_lock_fail count=1435
[ts 1612345678.124] thread=worker-27 sleep 0.00042s

Last thoughts:
- For a production rollout, opt for a hybrid default: paged attention on memory-constrained SKUs and fused path enabled for high-throughput dedicated clusters with sharded buffer pools and eviction backoff enabled. Flash remains good default on stable dedicated nodes but we need better allocator behavior.

If anyone reading has reproducible p99 traces that differ from mine, paste nvtx timeline + thread-switch sample and ping me in #eng-serving-runtime.
